newsitem.title: FRANCE: New Caledonia anti-separatist leader dies. [CORRECTED 14:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: New Caledonia anti-separatist leader dies. [CORRECTED 14:55 GMT]

text.p: New Caledonian anti-independence activist Maurice Nenou-Pwataho, a Gaullist parliamentarian for the French Pacific territory, has died in Noumea, officials said on Wednesday. (Corrects headline and text to show Nenou-Pwataho was against, not for, independence.)
In Paris, National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin called a minute's silence in honour of Nenou-Pwataho, 56, who entered parliament in 1986 and was regularly re-elected ever since.

Nenou-Pwataho was one of two deputies representing the territory -- the other is Gaullist Jacques Lafleur, leader of the anti-independence front. (Corrects to remove erroneous reference to Kanak pro-independence movement.)
A spokesman for the French consul-general in Sydney said Nenou-Pwataho "rejected extremist views in the debate over independence ... and had attempted to promote constructive dialogue".
A New Caledonian government delegation currently in Australia was cutting short its visit and returning home for Nenou-Pwataho's funeral on Friday.
